report.summary: Analyzed chunk 2 of 3 of daedalus/mapping/spectral.py: contains modularity_report, conductance_report, eigengap_report, and partial analyse function. All public symbols enumerated; docstring claims checked against visible code.
risks: modularity_report | medium | 'beats_random' compares declared > random_max, but docstring says 'Q >= 0.3 with clear lift' but no explicit check for lift > 0. | Check if docstring intends to check lift > 0 as well.

conductance_report | medium | 'leak_rate: None' when package is whole graph or no edges; docstring says 'reported with leak_rate: None' but also mentions 'reads_as' keys for those cases. | Verify that reads_as is set correctly for no-edge case.
eigengap_report | low | 'confident' uses gap > 1.5 * runner and gap > 0.02; docstring says 'meaningfully larger than the runner-up' but no threshold given. | Threshold is arbitrary; may need tuning.
todos: Check that 'reads_as' in conductance_report includes case for no edges (volume=0) with outside present.
Verify that 'beats_random' in modularity_report is computed as declared > random_max, not declared > random_mean.

claims.text: ``declared`` is Newman modularity Q of the on-disk package partition.
claims.why: Code computes declared = float(nx.community.modularity(graph, blocks)) using blocks from partition.

claims.text: ``random_mean`` is Q of partitions with the SAME block sizes and shuffled membership -- the null hypothesis, measured rather than assumed.
claims.why: Code shuffles nodes, splits by same sizes, computes modularity, and averages.

claims.text: ``lift`` is ``declared - random_mean``.
claims.why: Code computes lift = round(declared - random_mean, 6).

claims.text: Q >= 0.3 with clear lift -- the package layout is real structure.
claims.why: No code in chunk checks Q threshold or lift; only returns reads_as based on declared >= 0.3, 0.1, etc.

claims.text: lift <= 0 -- the declared layout is NO BETTER than shuffling the files.
claims.why: No explicit check for lift <= 0 in returned dict.

claims.text: Q < 0 -- worse than random: blocks are internally sparser than chance.
claims.why: No such classification in code.

claims.text: If graph.number_of_edges() == 0: return _unavailable('a graph with no edges has undefined modularity')
claims.why: Code has if graph.number_of_edges() == 0: return _unavailable(...).

claims.text: If len(blocks) < 2: return _unavailable('modularity needs at least 2 non-empty blocks')
claims.why: Code checks len(blocks) < 2 and returns that string.

claims.text: ``beats_random``: bool(declared > random_max)
claims.why: Code computes beats_random = bool(declared > random_max).

claims.text: ``reads_as``: based on declared thresholds 0.3, 0.1.
claims.why: Code computes reads_as using conditional on declared >= 0.3, >= 0.1, else 'filing...'.

claims.text: ``leak_rate`` is ``cut(S) / vol(S)`` -- of all the edge-endpoints this package has, the share that point outside it.
claims.why: Code computes leak = cut / volume.

claims.text: ``conductance_symmetric`` is textbook conductance, ``cut(S) / min(vol(S), vol(rest))``.
claims.why: Code computes symmetric = round(cut / floor, 6) where floor = min(volume, outside_volume).

claims.text: If graph.number_of_edges() == 0: return _unavailable('a graph with no edges has undefined conductance')
claims.why: Code has if graph.number_of_edges() == 0: return _unavailable(...).

claims.text: If not outside or volume == 0: rows.append with leak_rate = None, conductance_symmetric = None, reads_as = 'the package is the whole graph' or 'no edges at all'.
claims.why: Code checks not outside or volume == 0; sets leak_rate=None, symmetric=None, reads_as accordingly.

claims.text: Sorted worst-first, because the only reason to read this list is to find the top of it.
claims.why: Code sorts rows by -leak_rate (None treated as -1.0) then package name.

claims.text: ``reads_as`` in conductance: 'pass-through' if leak > 0.8, 'leaky' if >0.5, 'ordinary' if >0.2, else 'tight'.
claims.why: Code computes reads_as with those thresholds.

claims.text: The normalized Laplacian's eigenvalues are sorted ascending; the largest gap between consecutive eigenvalues at position k says 'there are k clusters'.
claims.why: Code sorts eigenvalues ascending, computes gaps, picks max gap, returns k.

claims.text: If n < 3: return _unavailable('a graph with fewer than 3 nodes has no cluster count')
claims.why: Code checks n < 3 and returns that string.

claims.text: If graph.number_of_edges() == 0: return _unavailable('a graph with no edges has no cluster structure')
claims.why: Code checks edges == 0 and returns that string.

claims.text: If components > 1: k, gap, runner = components, 0.0, 0.0; confident = True; reason = 'the graph is disconnected; the cluster count is the connected-component count by theorem, not by heuristic'.
claims.why: Code exactly does that.

claims.text: confident = bool(gap > 1.5 * runner and gap > 0.02) when graph is connected.
claims.why: Code sets confident = bool(gap > 1.5 * runner and gap > 0.02) in else branch.

claims.text: If declared_blocks is not None: out['reads_as'] based on comparison with k.
claims.why: Code checks declared_blocks is not None and sets reads_as accordingly.

claims.text: If components > 1: compute giant component spectrum and add to output.
claims.why: Code has if components > 1: giant = _giant(graph); if conditions met, compute scope values and add 'giant_component' key.

observations.what: Function analyse is incomplete; only signature present, no body in this chunk.
modularity_report uses _unavailable function which is not defined in this chunk.
conductance_report uses _unavailable function not defined in this chunk.
eigengap_report uses _unavailable and _giant functions not defined in this chunk.
modularity_report returns reads_as based on declared only, ignoring lift; docstring mentions lift but code does not use it.
conductance_report uses nx.volume, nx.cut_size, nx.subgraph; assumes graph is undirected.
eigengap_report uses nx.normalized_laplacian_spectrum; may raise for directed graphs.
modularity_report's 'beats_random' compares declared > random_max, not declared > random_mean as might be expected from docstring's 'lift <= 0' discussion.
